To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we present a new analysis of the Laplace distribution, (ii) we propose a new mechanism for histogram construction that eliminates the need for pre-defining the recursion depth, (iii) we demonstrate how the mechanism can be applied to spatial data and sequence data, and (iv) our experiments show that the mechanism outperforms the state-of-the-art solutions.

1) we present PrivTree that adopts hierarchical decomposition and eliminates the dependency on pre-defined h. 2) The core of Priv Tree is a new mechanism that exploits the analysis on Laplace distribution and enables us to use a constant amount of noises in deciding whether a domain should be split, which is crucial to eliminate the dependency on h. 3) We demonstrate the application in modelling spatial data and show that it is extendable to sequence data.
we present PrivTree: A differentially private algorithm for hierarchical decomposition that eliminates the need of a pre-defined recursion depth, by exploiting a new analysis on Laplace distribution.

the following questions: Given a set D containing n tuples over a domain Omega, what is the best way to construct a differentially private histogram over Omega to represent the tuple distribution in the dataset D?
the problem of how to construct a histogram over a domain Omega to approximate a tuple distribution in a set D of data tuples.
the problem of constructing a histogram from a set of tuples, with differential privacy guarantee.

we present a new differentially private algorithm for constructing histograms, which (i) is based on a new mechanism that eliminates the dependency on recursion depth in the hierarchical decomposition, and (ii) achieves better utility than existing approaches.

PrivTree is a differentially private algorithm for hierarchical decompositions that can construct a histogram of arbitrary precision, without the need of imposing a limit on the recursion depth.

we can achieve a high utility in histogram-based data release without having to sacrifice privacy.
